Republican incumbent [[Arne Carlson]] was term-limited and constitutionally ineligible to seek a third term in office. [[Reform Party of the United States of America|Reform Party]] candidate [[Jesse Ventura]], the former mayor of [[Brooklyn Park, Minnesota|Brooklyn Park]] and a former [[Professional wrestling|professional wrestler]], won office, defeating [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[Saint Paul, Minnesota|St. Paul]] mayor [[Norm Coleman]] and [[Minnesota Democratic–Farmer–Labor Party|DFL]] state attorney general [[Skip Humphrey]]. He succeeded Republican incumbent [[Arne Carlson]]. Ventura's victory as a third-party candidate was considered a historic major upset.{{cite web |last=Belluck |first=Pam |date=1998-11-05 |title=A 'Bad Boy' Wrestler's Unscripted Upset |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/11/05/us/the-1998-elections-the-states-the-maverick-a-bad-boy-wrestler-s-unscripted-upset.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20240103165849/https://www.nytimes.com/1998/11/05/us/the-1998-elections-the-states-the-maverick-a-bad-boy-wrestler-s-unscripted-upset.html |archive-date=2024-01-03 |access-date=2024-10-07 |work=The New York Times}} As of {{CURRENTYEAR}}, the election marks the only time a Reform Party candidate won a major government office. It also remains the last time a third-party candidate won any statewide election in Minnesota. Gubernatorial Race |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-srv/politics/campaigns/keyraces98/stories/ventura110498.htm |access-date=2024-10-07 |website=Washington Post}} The DFL primary saw candidates mostly focusing on issues, rather than attacking Humphrey. Humphrey had nearly lost the party's endorsement to Mike Freeman. The convention deadlock was broken when the labor caucus led by [[Minnesota Association of Professional Employees|MAPE]] delegate David Schmidt, endorsed Skip Humphrey pushing him over the top. The primary was nicknamed the "My Three Sons" campaign, owing to the political pedigree of three of the candidates, Freeman, Mondale and Humphrey. and Mark Dayton, heir to the Dayton fortune.{{Cite web |last=Jeter |first=Jon |date=September 17, 1998 |title=In Polite Race, Humphrey Kept Advantage |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-srv/politics/campaigns/keyraces98/stories/mn091798.htm |access-date=2024-10-07 |website=Washington Post}} Humphrey was endorsed by the [[Star Tribune]] in the run up to November. Coleman started as a strong challenger to Humphrey. Coleman received the Republican endorsement over more conservative candidates [[Allen Quist]] and [[Joanne Benson]]. Coleman ran as a social conservative, opposing abortion and gay marriage. He also campaigned on using the state's budget surplus to cut taxes, as well as expanding the state's school choice program to include [[school voucher]]s.{{Cite news |last=Belluck |first=Pam |date=October 31, 1998 |title=THE 1998 CAMPAIGN: MINNESOTA; Candidates Are Neck, Neck and Neck in Governor's Race |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/10/31/us/the-1998-campaign-minnesota-candidates-are-neck-neck-and-neck-in-governor-s-race.html |access-date=2024-10-07 |work=The New York Times}} Ventura spent around $300,000 and combined it with an aggressive [[grassroots]] campaign that featured a statewide bus tour, pioneered use of the Internet for political purposes, and aired quirky TV ads designed by [[Bill Hillsman]], who forged the phrase "Don't vote for politics as usual."{{cite web |last=Howey |first=Brian A. |title=Brian Howey: Time to Take Over the Indiana Libertarian Party |url=http://www.howeypolitics.com/2009/06/18/brian-howey-time-to-take-over-the-indiana-libertarian-party/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090818140106/http://www.howeypolitics.com/2009/06/18/brian-howey-time-to-take-over-the-indiana-libertarian-party/ |archive-date=2009-08-18 |access-date= |website=Howey Politics Indiana}} Unable to afford many television ads, Ventura mainly focused on televised debates and public appearances, preaching his brand of [[Libertarianism|libertarian]] politics. His speech at a parade in rural Minnesota during the summer attracted what organizers of the annual event described as one of its largest audiences. He ran on cutting taxes, reducing state government, and reducing public school classroom sizes to a 17 to 1 ratio. He also supported a public debate on the viability of legalized prostitution.{{cite news |last=Jeter |first=Jon |date=1998-10-22 |title='The Body' Slams Into Politics |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-srv/politics/campaigns/keyraces98/stories/mn102298.htm |access-date=2024-10-07 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]}} ===Polling=== A poll taken in June showed that Coleman would defeat any other Democratic candidate than Humphrey; Humphrey would defeat Coleman 44% to 34%. However, Ventura polled in the double digits. No other candidate in the Reform Party's brief history in Minnesota has received more than 5 percent of the votes in a statewide election.{{Cite web |last=Whereatt |first=Robert |date=1998-06-03 |title=Minnesota Poll: Humphrey holds lead in primary and general election races |url=http://www.startribune.com/local/11555066.html?elr=KArks8c7PaP3E77K_3c::D3aDhUMEaPc:E7_ec7PaP3iUeyc+D3aUUr |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110607062514/http://www.startribune.com/local/11555066.html?elr=KArks8c7PaP3E77K_3c::D3aDhUMEaPc:E7_ec7PaP3iUeyc+D3aUUr |archive-date=2011-06-07 |access-date= |website=[[Star Tribune]]}} Following the primary election in September, a poll on October 20 showed Humphrey leading 35% to Coleman (34%) and Ventura (21%). But the Star Tribune poll suggested that Ventura's surge with the voters had come mostly at Humphrey's expense. Since the primary, Humphrey's support among likely voters had dropped by 14 percentage points, while Coleman's had increased by 5 percentage points.{{Cite news |date=1998-10-12 |title=NEW POLL: HUMPHREY, COLEMAN IN DEAD HEAT |url=http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=PD&s_site=twincities&p_multi=SP&p_theme=realcities&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=0EB5E348CDCDBD3E&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D&s_trackval=GooglePM |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121020022307/http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=PD&s_site=twincities&p_multi=SP&p_theme=realcities&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=0EB5E348CDCDBD3E&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D&s_trackval=GooglePM |archive-date=2012-10-20 |work=St. Paul Pioneer Press |page=3B}} {| class="wikitable" style="font-size:90%;text-align:center;" |- valign=bottom !
